Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

itself pronoun

also by itself, of itself, the thing itself

classical

Cato Agr. 20.1: nē sē moveat
Cic. Sen. 52: ut sē ērigat

suī, sibi, sē (sēsē)

pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number

itself (as object), referring to the subject

For a thing as for a person: nē sē moveat, so that it doesn’t move (itself); ut sē ērigat, to raise itself. Many English “itself” verbs are plain verbs or passives in Latin (mōrēs sē dētegunt or mōrēs dēteguntur).

Other words

  • ipse, ipsa, ipsum — itself (for emphasis: the thing itself, of its own accord)

    pronoun, intensive · classical · Col. 12.2.6: ipse vacuus locus admonet; Plin. NH 18.104: ex ipsā farīnā

    Agrees in gender with the noun: ipse vacuus locus, the empty place itself; ex ipsā farīnā, from the flour itself; rēs ipsa, the thing itself. “By itself, of its own accord” is ipse or suā sponte (see own).

Examples

  • sī movēbitur, eximitō; dēnuō eōdem modō facitō, nē sē moveat

    If it moves, take it out; do it again the same way, so that it doesn’t move.Cato Agr. 20.1

  • vītis quidem, quae nātūrā cadūca est et, nisi fulta est, fertur ad terram, eadem, ut sē ērigat, claviculīs suīs quasi manibus quicquid est nacta complectitur

    The vine, which by nature droops and falls to the ground unless it is propped, raises itself by clasping with its tendrils, as with hands, whatever it finds.Cic. Sen. 52

  • omne animal sē ipsum dīligit

    every animal loves itselfCic. Fin. 5.9.24 (Lewis & Short)

  • sī quid forte abest, ipse vacuus locus admonet, ut, quod deest, requīrātur

    If anything happens to be missing, the empty place itself reminds you to look for what is lacking.Col. 12.2.6

  • nunc fermentum fit ex ipsā farīnā, quae subigitur priusquam addātur sāl, ad pultis modum dēcocta et relicta, dōnec acēscat

    Now leaven is made from the flour itself, which is kneaded before salt is added, boiled to a porridge and left until it turns sour.Plin. NH 18.104

  • dōnec quiētem ipse timor circumspectantibus aquam fēcisset

    until fear itself had made them keep still, as they looked round at the waterLiv. 21.28.11

See also it, its, himself, themselves.
